Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramirez (Redwood SE), Priya Gupta (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (VeloxSearch), Aisha Khan (VeloxSearch), Tom Hsu (VeloxSearch), Meera Patel (VeloxSearch)

Summary (auto): Demo of Redwood hosted embeddings and reranking endpoints for improving search relevance. Discussed telemetry, latency/cost tradeoffs, data residency, SOC2/KMS, and POC next steps. Agreed to run a 2-week POC once sample dataset provided.

00:00 Liam O'Connor: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh just a quick roll call. I'm Liam from Redwood, this is Sofia our solutions engineer, Priya is on for customer success.
00:12 Jordan Lee: Hey Liam, thanks, Jordan here, Aisha's on, Tom and Meera are on as well.
00:18 Sofia Ramirez: Great, we'll keep this focused on hosted API embeddings and the rerank flow. Quick agenda: show API calls, demo Console for model selection and Optimize recommendations, then talk POC.
00:35 Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Our main pain is ranking freshness and tail latency at 99p, we see bad reranks on long queries and cost is creeping up.
00:48 Sofia Ramirez: Yep, totally. We'll show a live example of embeddings -> semantic search -> rerank using the /embeddings and /rerank endpoints. Note: some of the transcript may garble acronyms, e.g., KV cache might show up as K-V cash in the notes.
01:05 Liam O'Connor: Quick qual — what's your current stack? Are you on Elastic or a hybrid approach?
01:12 Jordan Lee: We're on Elastic for inverted index, then a custom reranker built in-house that calls OpenAI for scoring today. Latency is inconsistent, and costs are spiking.
01:22 Tom Hsu: Also we run in GCP us-east1, need VPC peering options for the POC if possible.
01:28 Sofia Ramirez: Good to know. For hosted we support private networking options and mTLS, we also have Redwood Dedicated if you need reserved GPU pools later.
01:42 Meera Patel: Is there a big difference in model control between hosted and dedicated? We want to pin versions for rollout.
01:49 Sofia Ramirez: Hosted gives model version pinning too — you can pin to a model variant and use rollouts/canary policies via the Console. Dedicated adds capacity guarantees and network isolation. For POC hosted can be enough to validate quality/cost.
02:05 Jordan Lee: Ok, show us the actual API flow.
02:09 Sofia Ramirez: Sure. I'll share my screen — starting with embeddings. We send a POST to /v1/embeddings with the document batch, choose the embedding model, get vectors back. Then we do nearest-neighbor search in Velox's vector store, and pass the top N hits to /v1/rerank along with the query. Rerank returns a rescored list and explanation tokens if you enable structured output.
02:38 Jordan Lee: Do you support returning token-level attributions?
02:41 Sofia Ramirez: Yeah we have structured explanations in the rerank response — it's optional but helpful for debugging recency/relevance failures. Note: the structured output feature is still improving so sometimes the field names in the console look a bit off.
02:56 Aisha Khan: What about batching? At our scale we hit thousands QPS to the vector store and hundreds of rerank calls per second.
03:04 Sofia Ramirez: Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and cache profiles based on your traffic. For hosted, we do automatic prefix/KV caching and continuous batching to reduce per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs. You'll see suggested batch sizes in the Console under Optimize -> Recommendations.
03:27 Tom Hsu: We're particularly worried about 99th percentile latency — can you give a ballpark for embeddings + rerank in hosted mode?
03:34 Liam O'Connor: Ballpark depends on model and seq length. For a typical embeddings + small reranker model on hosted GPUs we often see tail latencies around 120-300ms rerank, embeddings under 40-80ms, so combined often in the sub-500ms region for many customers, but 99p can be higher during spikes. We'll run benchmarks for your workload.
04:01 Jordan Lee: How does that compare to calling OpenAI + our in-house? We're seeing 700-1,200ms right now.
04:07 Liam O'Connor: Very roughly, using our curated open models with optimized kernels often cuts that by half, and caching/prefix reuse helps a lot. Dedicated can reduce variability further.
04:21 Meera Patel: Security: we need SOC 2, KMS, audit logs and SSO.
04:26 Priya Gupta: Yep, we'll send the SOC 2 report and KMS integration docs — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and has audit-level logs per request in the Console. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported too.
04:40 Aisha Khan: Any concerns about data residency? We need EU-only storage for some content.
04:44 Sofia Ramirez: You can route requests to region-specific endpoints and we offer Private deploy for strict residency. Hosted supports storing data in regionally isolated storage based on your contract.
04:55 Jordan Lee: Ok demo part — can you run an example query?
05:00 Sofia Ramirez: Yep. I'm going to run a sample: query "best way to handle partial matches in product titles". I'll show the vector search hits then call rerank.
05:18 (screen click) Sofia Ramirez: Here's top-10 by cosine similarity — note some noise; after rerank, you'll see ordering improves to prioritize exact attribute matches.
05:32 Aisha Khan: Huh, that reorder looks good. Is rerank model supervised on our labels or generic zero-shot?
05:39 Sofia Ramirez: Both options — out-of-the-box zero-shot tends to work well, but you can fine-tune or provide labeled pairs to improve rerank. For hosted we support fine-tune-like approaches or learning-to-rank POC via our Optimize pipeline.
05:57 Jordan Lee: How do we instrument quality tests? We've got golden sets and NDCG targets.
06:02 Sofia Ramirez: Console includes per-route relevance dashboards and ties regressions to prompt sets/evals. You can set alerts for NDCG or other metrics. We'll show the Optimize tab after the API section.
06:18 (minor crosstalk)
06:25 Tom Hsu: On networking: do you provide VPC peering or private endpoints? We can't funnel traffic through the public internet for the POC.
06:33 Liam O'Connor: For hosted we can do VPC peering and private endpoints — it's a configuration we enable on the account. Dedicated/Private are alternatives if you need stricter isolation.
06:44 Jordan Lee: Let's talk cost — we need a rough TCO.
06:46 Liam O'Connor: We'll send curated TCO examples based on embeddings and rerank QPS, including estimates for caching hit rates and batching which drop token cost. Example in the pricing sheet we'll share.
06:59 Meera Patel: Can you show the Console quick?
07:03 Sofia Ramirez: Yep — Console shows per-model latency, cost per route, token breakdown, and Optimize recommendations. Here you can set rollout policies, pin model versions, and view trace links for slow requests.
07:22 Aisha Khan: Those trace links — do they include payloads for debugging?
07:25 Priya Gupta: They include request/response metadata and masked payloads depending on retention and privacy settings. Full payload retention is opt-in and covered under compliance.
07:39 Jordan Lee: For the rerank endpoint, what inputs do we send? Just query + doc snippets?
07:43 Sofia Ramirez: Query, candidate docs (id + snippet), optional metadata (e.g., recency score), and any context. The response includes scores, normalized rank, and optional explain tokens.
07:58 Aisha Khan: We frequently need freshness signals — can we include time-decay features?
08:02 Sofia Ramirez: Absolutely, you can pass metadata features and the reranker can use them as signals. For some clients we've integrated recency features into the reranker input and seen big wins.
08:18 Jordan Lee: Any limitations on candidate set size? We do top-100 retrieval then rerank top-50.
08:24 Sofia Ramirez: That's fine; rerank scales but cost grows with candidates. Optimize will recommend the sweet spot (often 10-50 depending on quality delta).
08:36 (pause)
08:42 Liam O'Connor: Quick objection we often hear — "why not just call OpenAI or Anthropic?" The short answer: you get more control, predictable cost via batching/caching, and unified tooling (Console + Optimize) for production rollouts.
08:58 Jordan Lee: Do you have customers who've replaced a multi-cloud OpenAI flow?
09:02 Liam O'Connor: Yes, several search-first companies moved from higher-latency external calls to our hosted runtimes and saw cost and latency improvements. We'll point to anonymized benchmarks.
09:14 Aisha Khan: Benchmarking — can you run our dataset through a sample and return 99p latency and NDCG?
09:19 Sofia Ramirez: Yes, that's the POC we propose: you give us data, we run a 2-week pilot with telemetry, and share metrics: throughput, 50/95/99p latency, cost per 1k queries, and relevance metrics.
09:36 Tom Hsu: Ok, network setup for the benchmark — we'll need a secure presigned S3 or internal repo.
09:41 Liam O'Connor: We'll provide secure upload instructions, and we can set up a dedicated API key scoped to the POC.
09:48 Meera Patel: Anything we should be careful about when preparing the dataset?
09:51 Sofia Ramirez: Please anonymize PII, include query timestamps for recency signals, and provide your golden labels for evaluation. If you can't share labels, we can run synthetic evaluations but labeled evals are best.
10:08 Jordan Lee: Great. Walkthrough wrap-up and next steps?
10:11 Liam O'Connor: Recap: we'll send pricing and compliance docs, Sofia will provision benchmark scripts + sample rerank notebook, Aisha will send dataset by 12/06, and we target POC kickoff week of 12/13.
10:26 Aisha Khan: Sounds good. One more quick thing — do you support model quantization or lower precision to save cost?
10:33 Sofia Ramirez: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles depending on your workload; our runtime supports quantized kernels to reduce memory and cost with small quality tradeoffs.
10:47 Jordan Lee: Ok thanks — any final questions?
10:50 (brief silence)
10:55 Priya Gupta: I'll follow up with SOC2, SSO, and the KB on KMS integrations.
11:02 Liam O'Connor: I'll email the pricing and set up a calendar invite for the POC kickoff. Sofia will add the benchmark repo link to the invite.
11:10 Meera Patel: Thanks all.
11:15 Jordan Lee: Thanks — look forward to the POC.
11:20 (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (VP-C for VPC), KV cache as K-V cash, some punctuation missing. Speakers occasionally overlap and speaker labels are correct for most turns but may be generic in auto-transcript export.
